learning_outcomes.text: The student can install an operating system (Linux and Windows) on a computer.
The student masters the concepts of the user interface, both graphical and command-line, to perform basic commands.
The student is able to connect at least 2 computers in a network in such a way that data can be shared between those machines.
The student is able to detect and correct defects in the configuration of an operating system.
The student can configure an operating system to ensure data security for different users of the system.
The student is able to install and configure software on Linux and Windows operating systems.
The student masters various storage techniques, both local and network-based, and can configure and combine them.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the Command Line Interface of Linux: basic commands
Networking: network configuration, connecting systems via network, sharing data between systems
Starting and stopping an operating system

assessment_methods.method: OS Fundamentals Lab (Practical exam and practical tests)

assessment_rules: The overall grade is on a scale of 1-20. The OS Fundamentals Theory and OS Fundamentals Lab components each account for 50% of the final grade. If a student scores less than 6/20 on either the Theory or Lab component, the maximum achievable grade for the entire course is 9/20. For the second examination opportunity, the same grading distribution applies, with both the written exam and practical test being re-examined. Passed partial results for Theory (YT6025) and Lab (YT6026) are transferable within the academic year.
bibliography: Nemeth, Snyder, Hein, Whaley. "Unix and Linux System Administration handbook". ISBN-13: 978-0-13-148005-6, ISBN-10: 0-13-148005-7
